title: Manus Automation in 2026: Free Tier, Pricing and Setup
summary: Manus automation translates plain English into automated jobs. Find pricing plans, free tier availability, and setup steps needed.
body_markdown:
## Schedule Manus tasks and connect apps


If the test run cost what you can live with, schedule it. Take the prompt that worked, set how often it runs, then point the output at email, Slack or a sheet.


I typed: "Every Monday at 8am, pull last week's new signups from the report I uploaded, summarize them in five bullets, and flag anything that dropped."


Then I set the schedule fields to match.


Keep the prompt identical to the one you tested. Rewording it "to make it better" means you're no longer running the task whose cost you measured.


Start with the slowest cadence you could tolerate, not the fastest.


> Keep the prompt identical to the one you tested. Rewording it "to make it better" means you're no longer running the task whose cost you measured.


**Every scheduled run draws on your credits** just like the test did, so a daily schedule burns through them far faster than a weekly one. Check your balance after the first two runs before you tighten the schedule, or you'll make it unworkably tight.


### Stage 5: Send results to email, Slack or a sheet


You have to remember to open a summary that sits inside Manus. Ask for delivery in the same plain English, and authorize each app when it prompts you:


- Email: "Send the summary to me at the end of each run."
- Slack: "Post it in the channel I name, with the flagged items first."
- A spreadsheet: "Add one row per run with the date and the key numbers."


Pick one destination first. Each connection is another thing that can break quietly, and a run that fails at the delivery step still used credits.


If you need something the built-in connections don't cover, Manus also exposes an API, which suits you only if you're comfortable with a little code.


### When to add a workflow automation tool


Add one when the job should start because something happened, such as a new form entry or a new customer, not because the clock says Monday. A scheduler can't do that.


In the dialog below, you name the connection, choose which projects may use it, and paste in an API key for the service, here Drip, an email marketing platform whose key comes from its account settings page.


Before you pay for the extra tool, know that it means doing that setup, and it's only worth it when you need event-driven runs.


A job that starts on a new form entry or a new row is where[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) can sit around Manus, calling it and routing the result onward.


Manus credits are consumed by task complexity and duration, so a ten-step flow can cost more than the two-step shortcut it replaced.


Zapier's per-task billing and Make's per-module billing work the other way, charging more as the flow gets finer.


For a plain weekly report, skip it and keep everything inside Manus, where you only have one set of limits to watch.
